the institutional environment in sub-Saharan Africa does not have to be high-quality, as long as managers are willing and able to make informal payments.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
managers can make up for the lack of quality institutions in their environment.
managers have to spend effort and make informal payments in order to make the best of a low-quality institutional environment.
, in the presence of high-quality institutions, managers should spend effort to navigate the institutional environment, and firms should not make informal payments to the authorities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the industrial development in sub-Sahara Africa is more affected by the institutional environment than that of other countries.
